repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
fired := false
if (fired == true) {
wait until((#K_Leak).leakSensor_leakage == false)
fired = false
}
wait until((#K_Leak).leakSensor_leakage == true)
(#K_Cam).camera_startRecording()
fired = true

diagnosis.summary: The candidate implements a periodic `if` check at the start of the wrapper period, whereas the IR requires a rising-edge wait that blocks until the condition transitions from false to true. The candidate fails to fire if the leakage is already true at t=0 (missing the initial rising edge) and fails to fire if the transition occurs mid-period (missed by the periodic guard).
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic `if` guard with the standard rising-edge state machine: persist a `fired` flag, block until the condition is false if previously fired, then block until the condition is true, execute the body, and mark as fired. This ensures the action fires exactly on the rising edge and respects the 1 SEC cycle period between completions.
